sampled:
power: eruptions this bright only happen about every 100,000 years on Earth.

The explosions, known as suicidals, come from an eruption at the summit of the volcano, one of the most powerful in history. The eruptions are so bright because their explosive gas and lava are superheated to millions of degrees. Scientists can compare the eruptions to the nuclear blasts that happened in the 1950s and 1960s in the Nevada desert.

Suicidal eruptions are rare, but not unprecedented: Only two other volcanoes in the world -- the Yellowstone Caldera in Wyoming and the Mount St. Helens volcano in Washington state -- have had eruptions that were at least as bright as the ones at Kilauea.

The eruptions are so bright that the entire Hawaiian Islands were seen from the surface of the moon, NASA scientists reported in 2001.
